subject: Request: Architecture proof-of-fit session & agenda alignment
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlashealth.ai>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Architecture proof-of-fit session & agenda alignment

Hi Samira + Tom —

Thanks again for the discovery call yesterday — really useful context on the latency and privacy constraints for your outpatient triage pipeline. I put together a short proposal for a focused architecture proof-of-fit session so we can validate the end-to-end inference path and identify any integration gaps ahead of a pilot.

High-level ask: 60-minute technical session with your infra/SRE and security counterparts + our Solutions Engineer. Goal is to walk through:
- current request patterns and p99 latency targets
- data flow (ingest -> preprocessing -> inference -> postprocessing) and where keys/caching live
- quantization/throughput tradeoffs and deployment topology options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- any compliance points (audit logs, KMS) that could affect deployment timeline

Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue Nov 9, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed Nov 10, 11:00–12:00 PT (partial availability)
- Thu Nov 11, 13:00–14:00 PT

I attached a one-page pre-read of my notes from discovery (discovery-notes-Atlas-20261104.pdf) — please scan and tell me if you'd like me to focus the session on any single item. Also let me know who from your side should join (SRE, security, data platform).

If those windows work, I can loop in Ben (SE) and Marissa (CS) to finalize agenda and deliverables.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com
+1 415-555-0172

Attachments: discovery-notes-Atlas-20261104.pdf
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlashealth.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Architecture proof-of-fit session & agenda alignment

Diego —

Appreciate the clear agenda. Tue Nov 9, 10:00–11:00 PT works for me and Tom. We'll plan to invite: 
- Priya Menon (SRE lead)
- Carlos Vega (Data Platform)
- Sophie Liu (Security/compliance) — she will want to confirm KMS and audit log timelines.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you include any brief checklist around network egress and VPC peering patterns you expect for a Private deployment? Sophie will want that ahead of time.
- If your SE can bring recommended sizing options for 8–16 concurrent sessions with 2x p99 spikes, that would be helpful.

I don't have Tom's calendar blocked yet — if you confirm Tue 10 PT I'll accept.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, Atlas Health
samira.khan@atlashealth.ai
+1 617-555-9901

Excellent — thanks Samira. I'm marking Tue Nov 9, 10:00–11:00 PT as our working slot. Ben, can you lead the session for Redwood and bring the sizing/recommendations Samira asked for? Below are items to prep so we can use the hour efficiently: 

Ben (SE) prep requests:
- brief slide with topology options for hosted/dedicated/private (single slide each)
- recommended instance sizing and expected p99 throughput for 8–16 concurrent sessions + typical batching assumptions
- network/VPC checklist (e.g., egress, firewall rules, peering options) — Sophie will want this beforehand
- short runbook bullets for fallback model variants / graceful degradation if capacity spikes

Marissa, can you own sending the calendar invite (Google Meet) and include the pre-read + Ben's one-slide attachments once he posts them?

Samira: attaching a Redwood ops checklist that addresses common network/KMS items — redwood-ops-compatibility-checklist.xlsx. If Sophie wants anything more formal we can turn it into a short compliance artifact.

Diego Fernandez

Hi Samira, Tom —

Thanks for the context — I'll take point for Redwood on Tue Nov 9. Quick note on format so you know what to expect:
- 45 minutes walkthrough (topology + sizing + integration checklist)
- 15 minutes Q&A and next-step assignment (pilot kickoff criteria)

I've attached a short draft playbook that covers our recommended topologies and a baseline sizing matrix for the concurrency profile you shared (architecture-playbook-draft.pdf). Highlights I will walk through:
- Hosted API tradeoffs (latency vs cost) and when to recommend Dedicated
- Private deployment network patterns (VPC peering vs private link) and KMS models
- KV cache and batching heuristics that impact p99
- Runbook steps for safe rollout and rollback during pilot

If Sophie or Priya want any extra artifacts (e.g., sample IAM policies or example peering configs), tell me now and I'll include them in the invite.

I'll hand the calendar over to Marissa for the invite; please watch for a Google Meet link shortly.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood-inference.com

Attachments: architecture-playbook-draft.pdf
